Subject: Request: on-prem VPC topology sanity check for StratusCloud

Hi Maya,

Hope you're well — we have an upcoming on-prem rollout for a customer PoC in the NYC colo and we'd like Redwood to run a quick topology sanity check before we lock the network changes. High-level ask: validate control-plane/data-plane separation, egress rules, and any obvious MTU/NAT issues that could break KV cache replication.

I've attached our current diagram and inventory (stratus-topology-v1.pdf, network-inventory.xlsx). Can you and your team review and propose a short checklist + a 60-minute readout? Prefer the check this week or early next week.

Attendees from our side: myself (Tim Hayes), ops-eng@stratuscloud.com (network team).

Thanks — Tim

Thanks Tim — saw the attachments, helpful.

Proposed output from our end:

- Short runbook/checklist you can run during the cut (15–20 checks)

Suggested agenda for the readout (60 min):

4) Egress & NAT/MTU pitfalls (10 min)
5) Runbook & canary plan (10 min)

Would like to include Karthik (serving/runtime-network) and Irene (deployment/ops) on the call — cc'd.

We attached a Redwood reference diagram and a short control-plane checklist to speed review (redwood-vpc-reference-20260929.pdf, controlplane-auth-checklist.md). If you can share the firewall rules export or CSR/NAT table before the call that would be ideal.

Quick notes from the runtime/network perspective:
- Control plane auth: confirm TLS termination point and whether customer will provide a customer-managed KMS/HSM for key material. If KMS is customer-managed, we need IAM mappings and a reachable endpoint from the control plane.
- Data plane egress: verify whether outgoing traffic to external services (metrics, S3) needs to traverse the colo egress or can go via Redwood-managed egress. This affects firewall rules and NAT allocations.
- KV cache replication: check for symmetric routing between nodes; asymmetric SNAT can cause stale KV sessions if packets take different egress paths.
- MTU/NAT: ask ops to run ping -s tests between nodes for jumbo frames; note any VXLAN overlays that could reduce effective MTU.

I'll prep a minimal canary plan we can suggest during the call (pin one model, traffic-weighting to 1%, smoke tests on generation latency + KV consistency). Draft attached.

Karthik
